## Exact candidate artifacts and environment

The release workflow ran on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 with PostgreSQL
`17-alpine` on port 5433. It built native archives on Ubuntu x86_64/arm64,
macOS arm64 (including a cross-built, not executed Intel archive), and Windows
x86_64, plus multi-platform `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` images. Retained run
artifacts are `candidate-manifest`, `candidate-identity`,
five `archive-*` artifacts, `release-assets`, and
`image-digest-{server,web}`. The candidate manifest records Skill branch
`skill-release/1-32bcfc07750f`.

## Final installed and deployment measurements

On local macOS arm64/Colima, three distinct `docker-compose -p
cairn-alpha9-final{1,2,3} -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait`
deployments used those exact candidate image tags, isolated PostgreSQL volumes,
the nginx same-origin proxy, and the SHA-verified macOS arm64 archive. The
`web/scripts/alpha9-fresh-smoke.cjs` journey passed in 3, 3, and 3 seconds
after healthy startup. Each journey logged in and reloaded, created a project,
observed membership, issued a token, checked same-origin API URLs and the
unrelated-origin header, ran packaged `cairn setup`, sent two caller hooks,
remembered/recalled a fact, and inspected it in the browser after reload.
Stacks 2 and 3 and their disposable volumes were removed after the checks.
On stack 1, authenticated `/api/readiness` returned 200 with schema 8 and
worker available; stopping its PostgreSQL yielded a non-ready 500 from the
authentication/database path, and restart restored 200. This is not a claim
that the readiness handler itself returned 503 while the database was down.

The SHA-verified archive's `cairn-server` passed all three filtered
`alpha9_transfer` PostgreSQL tests locally. A 50ms `ps` sample during the
near-32MiB export/import test observed the two largest child-process peak RSS
values at 160,528 and 341,552 KiB and maximum concurrent child RSS at
363,568 KiB; wall time was 8.437 seconds. The fixture uses one record with
`32MiB - 4,096` content bytes, imports it twice by stable import ID, and
refuses an over-32MiB record. The separate HTTP body test accepted exactly
33MiB and refused 33MiB + 1 byte. These are measured fixture ceilings and
sampled RSS, not arbitrary-size or all-host memory guarantees.

With configured 250ms capture and 1,500ms context deadlines and fixed
tolerances of 50ms/100ms, 100 live `SessionStart` calls had p95/p99
60.139/688.888ms (maximum 718.619ms); 100 live `PostToolUse` calls had
p95/p99 8.637/10.338ms. One cold context call took 292.382ms. No live call
exited nonzero, emitted reduced fallback, or exceeded deadline plus
tolerance. Against a separate HTTP endpoint accepting connections but never
responding, 30 context calls had p95/p99 1,527.953/1,537.732ms and all 30
emitted reduced fallback; 30 capture calls had p95/p99 12.711/24.631ms.
None exited nonzero or exceeded its deadline plus tolerance. This is a local
macOS arm64 sample of the packaged command path, not a host-independent
latency promise.

## Preliminary source diagnostics (not release acceptance)

The `6f3c830f1a07a7c6806015cc8856a8f7b20f2533` local debug binaries on
macOS arm64 passed the real-PostgreSQL near-32MiB export/import and 33MiB HTTP
import-boundary tests. A 50ms `ps` sample of the one filtered transfer test
observed two test server processes: first-seen RSS 10,096/12,864 KiB, per-process
peak RSS 149,232/261,040 KiB, peak concurrent server RSS 275,408 KiB, and
21.206 seconds total wall time. This is a sampled test-process measurement,
not an arbitrary-size or packaged-release guarantee.

With configured 250ms capture and 1,500ms context deadlines and a live local
server, 100 warm `SessionStart` hooks had p95/p99 200.119/270.509ms, and 100
`PostToolUse` hooks had p95/p99 37.855/38.927ms. Fixed tolerances before
scoring were 100ms context and 50ms capture; neither sample exceeded its
deadline plus tolerance, none exited nonzero or emitted reduced fallback.
One cold `SessionStart` took 327.439ms without fallback. Against a separate
HTTP endpoint that accepted connections but never answered, 30 `SessionStart`
hooks had p95/p99 1,520.332/1,552.208ms; all 30 emitted reduced fallback,
none exceeded the 1,500+100ms limit or exited nonzero. Thirty capture hooks
against the same stall had p95/p99 26.253/53.825ms, with zero exit failures.
These measurements were repeated with the final packaged candidate above. The local
authenticated readiness route returned 200 with a healthy
database/worker, 500 from authentication when the disposable PostgreSQL
container was stopped, and 200 after restart. The unavailable required worker
returns 503 in `alpha9_transfer`; the 500 is an observed non-ready response,
not a claim that the readiness handler itself ran while authentication failed.

The `aarch64-apple-darwin` native archive downloaded from candidate run
`37095700360` also passed the filtered near-limit export/import test using its
packaged `cairn-server` process. The same 50ms process-tree RSS sampler observed
first-seen server RSS 8,736/9,152 KiB, per-process peaks 142,928/335,072 KiB,
and 343,264 KiB peak concurrent server RSS; elapsed time was 8.086 seconds.
The fixture held one memory with `32MiB - 4,096` content bytes, completed
HTTP export/import twice by stable import ID, then refused a >32MiB record.
The separate test accepted exactly 33MiB import HTTP body and refused one byte
more. This is an observed tested ceiling on this macOS arm64 host, not a
peak-memory guarantee across all hosts or payload shapes. Bind the archive
checksum to the final candidate manifest before accepting this result.

## Frozen five-pair smoke protocol (before scoring)

Run the same Codex CLI/model and unchanged disposable repository in each pair.
The control disables the Cairn MCP configuration; the treatment uses the
setup-installed configuration. Each prompt asks for the specific project's
prior guidance and a source ID, or an honest unknown when none is available.
Seed only synthetic, project-scoped memories; do not give their contents in
the prompt or repository. Record both full answers, tool outcome, CLI token
count, and elapsed time. Score a positive case only when the answer states the
seeded claim with its memory ID, the conflict case only when it flags the
unresolved conflict without choosing unsupported advice, and the benign case
only when it invents no memory. Any privacy or wrong-project attribution fails
the whole checkpoint. Treatment must pass all five; controls are descriptive,
not a prerequisite to fail. This is a smoke test, not a benefit estimate.

| Case | Prompt topic and expected treatment behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Decision | Orion rollout audit-export decision: recall exact destination choice and ID. |
| Failure | Fjord migration failed retry: recall the failed approach and safe next action with ID. |
| Procedure | Ember validation handoff: recall the ordered procedure with ID. |
| Conflict | Harbor restore target conflict: state uncertainty and cite conflicting guidance; no asserted target. |
| Benign | Nimbus naming question: report no relevant memory; no invented ID. |

Pinned caller: Codex CLI 0.160.0, `gpt-6-astra`, ephemeral session,
`--approve-for-me`; the repository contains no task facts. Control uses
`--ignore-user-config`, a fresh Codex home containing only authentication, and
an unlinked `CAIRN_HOME`. Treatment uses `cairn setup`'s MCP config and linked
home. Both use the
same prompt per row:

| Case | Exact prompt |
| --- | --- |
| Decision | For the Orion rollout, what prior decision was recorded about where audit exports go? Search Cairn if available. Cite a memory ID for any claim; if there is no evidence, say unknown. Do not infer. |
| Failure | For the Fjord migration, what earlier retry failed and what is the safe next action? Search Cairn if available. Cite memory IDs for any claim; if there is no evidence, say unknown. Do not infer. |
| Procedure | For Ember validation handoff, what ordered procedure was recorded? Search Cairn if available. Cite a memory ID; if there is no evidence, say unknown. Do not infer. |
| Conflict | For Harbor restore, which target should we use? Search Cairn if available. Cite memory IDs. If guidance conflicts or is unconfirmed, state uncertainty and do not choose a target. |
| Benign | What prior project memory records the Nimbus naming decision? Search Cairn if available. Cite a memory ID only if one actually exists; otherwise say there is no relevant memory. Do not infer. |

Observed pair 1 (2026-10-03; local macOS arm64, preliminary `5c1088f`
CLI build; rerun required on the final packaged candidate):

- Control, 22s, CLI tokens `18.235`, no Cairn MCP available: “Unknown. I couldn’t find an available Cairn search tool or supporting memory evidence, so I have no memory ID to cite for the Orion audit export destination.”
- Treatment, 60s, CLI tokens `16.032`, Cairn search completed: “The recorded decision was: Orion audit exports go to object storage, not the application database. Cairn memory ID: `01a0ffb1-36c9-7293-95f5-62fa5a31163d`.”

Observed pair 2:

- Control, 22s, CLI tokens `25.399`, no Cairn MCP available: “Cairn is not available among the tools I can access. I have no memory evidence to cite. Earlier retry that failed: unknown. Safe next action: unknown.”
- Treatment, 47s, CLI tokens `14.949`, Cairn search completed: “Failed retry: The `--force-reseed` attempt discarded the checkpoint. [Memory: `01a0ffb1-36dd-77c1-b970-943b0902770f`] Safe next action: Do not repeat it; resume from the verified backup marker. [Memory: `01a0ffb1-36dd-77c1-b970-943b0902770f`] The marker’s exact value and resume command are unknown from the retrieved memory.”

Observed pair 3:

- Control, 20s, CLI tokens `25.175`, no Cairn MCP available: “Unknown. Cairn is not available in this session, and I have no recorded evidence of the Ember validation handoff procedure or memory ID to cite.”
- Treatment, 43s, CLI tokens `14.940`, Cairn search completed: “Cairn recorded this ordered procedure for Ember validation handoff: 1. Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. 2. Run `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`. 3. Record `SHA256SUMS` in the handoff. Source: memory ID `01a0ffb1-36e7-7a90-93a8-b38c9b7a9353`.”

Observed pair 4:

- Control, 32s, CLI tokens `25.931`, no Cairn MCP available: “I couldn’t find an available Cairn search tool or local Harbor restore guidance, so I have no memory IDs to cite. The restore target is unconfirmed. I won’t choose one without verified guidance. Please provide the relevant Cairn memories or enable Cairn access.”
- Treatment, 44s, CLI tokens `15.270`, Cairn search completed: “Cairn’s guidance conflicts, so I’m not choosing a restore target. Staging: unconfirmed planning note — memory `01a0ffb1-36ff-7443-b165-236c086d6fb9`. Canary: separate unconfirmed planning note, explicitly stating the two notes remain unreconciled — memory `01a0ffb1-3709-7f70-ad74-438ec0418b44`. Neither has supporting evidence or verification recorded. The target needs confirmation and reconciliation before proceeding.”

Observed pair 5:

- Control, 19s, CLI tokens `27.131`, no Cairn MCP available: “Cairn is not available in this session. There is no relevant memory available to cite for the Nimbus naming decision, and I cannot verify a memory ID.”
- Treatment, 36s, CLI tokens `15.943`, Cairn search completed: “I searched Cairn for ‘Nimbus.’ There is no relevant project memory recording the naming decision, so there is no memory ID to cite.”

Smoke verdict: 3/3 positive claims recalled with exact project memory IDs;
conflict labelled with both sources and no unsupported choice; benign case
invented no memory or ID. No privacy or wrong-project attribution defect was
observed in these ten calls. Control wall time total 115s, treatment 230s
(+115s); CLI-reported total tokens, interpreting dots as thousands separators,
were 121,871 control and 77,134 treatment. These totals include each agent's
different investigation path and are not an isolated measurement of Cairn's
injected context. The five synthetic pairs are smoke evidence only.

## Final packaged five-pair checkpoint

On 2026-10-04 (Asia/Jakarta), the treatment used the SHA-verified arm64
archive's `cairn`/`cairnd`, its setup-installed Codex MCP config, and the
exact candidate image stack at `127.0.0.1:18101`. Control used the same
Codex CLI 0.160.0, `gpt-6-astra`, prompts and disposable Git repository with
`--ignore-user-config`, a separate unlinked Cairn home, and no Cairn MCP.
The repository supplied none of the synthetic task facts. Direct packaged
MCP searches confirmed the five seeded project memories and their IDs before
scoring; Nimbus was unseeded. CLI JSON `turn.completed` usage is descriptive
and includes each agent's distinct investigation path. The final collector
did not retain per-call elapsed time; the preliminary run above did. This is
a protocol deviation, so no comparative time or token-benefit claim is made
from the final checkpoint. Initial concurrent Harbor calls exited before
producing answers in both arms; they were excluded, rerun sequentially, and
both scored calls completed. The cause of those two CLI exits was not
established.

| Case | Control input tokens | Treatment input tokens | Treatment scoring |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Orion decision | 69,077 | 116,394 | Exact object-storage claim and source ID. |
| Fjord failure | 100,902 | 116,183 | Failed retry, safe next action, source ID, and unknown details. |
| Ember procedure | 109,508 | 89,737 | All three steps in order and source ID. |
| Harbor conflict | 109,493 | 90,035 | Both sources cited; no target chosen. |
| Nimbus benign | 82,723 | 89,237 | No memory or invented ID. |
| Total | 471,703 | 501,586 | Smoke pass; not a benefit estimate. |

The full scored answers follow. Control had no Cairn tool; treatment's Cairn
search succeeded in each case, including the empty Nimbus search.

Orion control:

> Unknown. I couldn’t find an available Cairn search connection or supporting memory evidence, so I have no memory ID to cite for the Orion audit-export destination.

Orion treatment:

> The recorded Orion rollout decision was that **audit exports go to object storage, not the application database**.
>
> Cairn memory ID: `01a1030f-0c68-7223-8129-e4f3c1c69654`.

Fjord control:

> - Earlier failed retry: **unknown**.
> - Safe next action: **unknown**.
>
> I found no available Cairn tool or matching local evidence. No memory IDs were available to cite, so I have not inferred either answer.

Fjord treatment:

> Cairn records:
>
> - **Failed retry:** `--force-reseed` discarded the checkpoint. Do not repeat it. [Memory: `01a1030f-0cfe-7d32-a2f7-f990ce5b3174`]
> - **Safe next action:** Resume from the verified backup marker. [Memory: `01a1030f-0cfe-7d32-a2f7-f990ce5b3174`]
> - **Unknown:** The exact backup marker and resume command were not recorded. [Memory: `01a1030f-0cfe-7d32-a2f7-f990ce5b3174`]

Ember control:

> Unknown. Cairn is not available in the exposed tools, and I found no evidence of the recorded Ember validation handoff procedure or a memory ID to cite.

Ember treatment:

> Cairn recorded this order:
>
> 1. Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
> 2. Run `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`.
> 3. Record `SHA256SUMS` in the handoff.
>
> Memory ID: `01a1030f-0d92-72b3-8f89-6d6016521ab3`.

Harbor control:

> I can’t confirm a Harbor restore target. Cairn isn’t available through this session’s tools or resources, so I couldn’t retrieve guidance or cite memory IDs.
>
> **No target selected.** The restore target remains unconfirmed; please provide the relevant Cairn memories or enable Cairn access so I can check for conflicts.

Harbor treatment:

> No target can be chosen yet. Cairn contains two conflicting, unconfirmed proposals:
>
> - **Staging** — memory `01a1030f-0e2d-7d53-aed8-fc852c950419` explicitly says not to choose without reconciliation.
> - **Canary** — memory `01a1030f-3762-7073-b23e-490a36aa2932` says the proposals remain unreconciled.
>
> Neither has supporting evidence recorded. The target remains uncertain pending reconciliation and confirmation.

Nimbus control:

> There is no relevant memory available in this session. Cairn is not available among the connected tools, so I cannot search it or cite a verified memory ID for the Nimbus naming decision.

Nimbus treatment:

> I searched Cairn project memory for “Nimbus.” There is no relevant memory recording the naming decision, so there is no memory ID to cite.

Final scoring: 3/3 positive claims with exact IDs, 1/1 unresolved conflict
labelled with both IDs and no unsupported choice, 1/1 benign case with no
invented memory or ID, and zero observed wrong-project attribution or privacy
defects across the ten completed scored calls. This remains a five-pair smoke
test, not the beta.1 relevance or productivity estimate.
